title: [CQ-V12a] Delivery bypass acceptance fixtures
description:
Objective: daemon-side, end-to-end proof that forged, stale, missing, target-raced or crash-replayed evidence cannot pass the CQ-V gates. This is V12's DoD 1, split out of the epic-final V12 (task-b621ddc9) on 2026-10-29 by architect-e4b7eee0 for size. V12 keeps the docs sweep, the whole-epic review and regression, and re-runs these fixtures unchanged.

Deliverable:
- A new packages/moe-daemon/src/__acceptance__/deliveryBypass.acceptance.test.ts built on CQ-V11's harness (src/__acceptance__/mcpCall.ts: createMcpCaller, McpCallError, the gatedApproval scenario of producerConsumer.acceptance.test.ts). Every call goes through McpAdapter, never an imported handler.
- The two CQ-V01 QA hand-forward tests in src/delivery/requiredChecks.delivery.test.ts. They are spelled out in V12's comment from qa-7c627d35 (2026-10-26).

Fixture classes, all on a STRICT task:
- A verified-local task is built the way CQ-V06's reviewBinding.test.ts and src/__e2e__/executionContract.e2e.test.ts drive one. The readiness gate (assertExecutionProfileReady) is spied ONLY inside the test; the precedent is src/server/planApproval.test.ts:1095. Production readiness stays unconditionally unavailable.
- Forgery: a /mcp record_check_run claiming runner-observed; record_check_dispatch or record_check_observation without the /runner context; observation args carrying runnerId, source, candidateId, treeSha or planRevision.
- Stale: a passing run on a superseded candidate, an older plan revision, or a stale served-context receipt.
- Missing check: missing, skipped, inconclusive, timeout and infra-failure results, and an exit-0 run followed by a tree, index or HEAD mutation (CQ-V04).
- Target race and receipt crash, daemon side: a receipt or landing record for a tree other than the verified candidate's; an identical receipt replayed after a fresh StateManager load over the same .moe directory.
- At least one case runs over the real /runner WebSocket with a host key in a temp MOE_RUNNER_KEY_DIR (CQ-V03a). A wrong or missing key is refused at upgrade.

Assumed interfaces, from approved plans; adapt to the LANDED names:
- V03a: server/runnerChannel.ts (RUNNER_KEY_HEADER, ensureRunnerKey, authenticateRunner), ToolCallContext.runner.
- V03b: state/checkObservationStore.ts (recordCheckDispatch, recordCheckObservation, isAuthenticatedCheckRun).
- V03 tools: moe.record_check_dispatch and moe.record_check_observation.
- V04's dispatch flow, which is unplanned at the time of writing.
- V06: delivery/reviewBinding.ts (assertReviewedCandidateCurrent), and qa_approve's attemptId, generation, sessionId and candidateId.
- V05b's repair transitions.
- moe.record_delivery_receipt and moe.finalize_attempt.

Error handling: assert exact codeNames and tokens, never truthiness. A bypass a fixture exposes is fixed at its source module, with that fixture as the regression, never by weakening the fixture.

Scope boundaries: no new production surface beyond such fixes; no client UI; no wrapper changes (CQ-V08b owns those); no .moe edits; verified-local stays unavailable outside test spies.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test
definitionOfDone: Forgery: a /mcp record_check_run claiming runner-observed, a dispatch or observation sent without the /runner context, and observation args carrying runnerId/source/candidateId each leave a strict task's qa_approve refused, with exact codeNames and tokens asserted, proven by src/__acceptance__/deliveryBypass.acceptance.test.ts.
Stale: a passing run on a superseded candidate, on an older plan revision, or under a stale served-context receipt cannot satisfy qa_approve, with each exact codeName asserted in the same file.

Missing check: missing, skipped, inconclusive, timeout and infra-failure required checks, and an exit-0 run followed by a tree/index/HEAD mutation, each keep qa_approve refused, proven in the same file.

Target race and receipt crash, daemon side: a receipt for a tree other than the verified candidate's never satisfies delivery evidence or a strict consumer's dependency, and an identical receipt replayed after a fresh StateManager load is idempotent with dependents unchanged, proven in the same file.
At least one case runs over the real /runner WebSocket with a host key (a wrong or missing key is refused at upgrade); every other case goes only through createMcpCaller.

The two CQ-V01 hand-forward tests in requiredChecks.delivery.test.ts (a corrupt requiredChecks entry gives protected-checks-unapproved; a duplicate candidate protected path, first or last, gives protected-checks-unmeasured) each kill their named mutant on a scratch copy.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits 0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 6: the two CQ-V01 QA hand-forward tests, in packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/requiredChecks.delivery.test.ts. They are spelled out in qa-7c627d35's 2026-10-26 comment on V12 (task-b621ddc9). Reuse the file's own helpers: task(), missing(), candidate(treeSha, protectedEntries, runs), defs, OID and the deliveryProjection read the other cases use. Add no new fixture machinery.

1. `it('fails closed on a corrupt requiredChecks entry')`:
   - set h.state.tasks.set('task-1', { ...task(), executionContract: { requiredChecks: [{ ...defs[0], bogus: 1 }, defs[1]] } });
   - expect missing() toStrictEqual ['protected-checks-unapproved'];
   - expect the projection's requiredCheckSatisfied to be false.
2. `it.each(['first', 'last'])('reads a duplicate candidate protected path as unmeasured (%s)')`: a candidate whose protectedEntries repeat entries[0].path with oid OID, placed first and then last. In both cases missing() toStrictEqual ['protected-checks-unmeasured'].

Kill the named mutants on a scratch copy, restore it, then cmp:
- `return []` in protectedCheckShortfall's validateExecutionContract catch (delivery/policy.ts) must fail test 1;
- dropping protectedDrift's `candidate.has(path)` guard must fail both rows of test 2.

Record both mutant results in the step note. These are tests: no production edit in this step.

Iterate with `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/delivery/requiredChecks.delivery.test.ts`.

packages/moe-daemon/src/__acceptance__/mcpCall.ts was created by CQ-V11. It is listed as new only because it does not exist at plan time: edit it, never recreate it.

Give createMcpCaller an optional third parameter, `options: McpHandleOptions = {}` (the type exported by server/McpAdapter.ts), and forward it to EVERY adapter.handle call: `adapter.handle(request, options)`.

This is how an acceptance test reaches the runner-only tools through the same dispatch the /runner endpoint uses. WebSocketServer.handleMcpMessage calls mcpAdapter.handle(request, { runner }).

Add one header sentence:
- options.runner must come from authenticateRunner over the temp host key, never from a literal;
- the real /runner upgrade is proven separately (server/runnerChannel.test.ts W1, and this task's W1 case).

Error handling is unchanged: McpCallError keeps code and codeName. With no third argument, existing callers keep exactly today's behavior.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, once, as the last step. Load adversarial-self-review. Read the diff as an agent who wants a fixture to pass without testing anything:
- vacuity: every refusal case must differ from A0 by exactly one defect, and assert the exact codeName and exact tokens. A refusal for the wrong reason, such as a missing identity, must fail the case.
- dispatch path: grep the acceptance file for 'Tool(' and '.handler(': there must be no hits. Every call goes through createMcpCaller, apart from the W1 WebSocket.
- trust: the runner identity comes only from authenticateRunner over the temp host key; the key appears in no log line or assertion message; MOE_RUNNER_KEY_DIR is restored.
- isolation: the readiness spy is restored in afterEach, and P0 pins production readiness. Restarts rebuild both callers; servers and sockets are closed on every path.
- rails: verified-local stays unavailable outside the spy; no .moe edits, no Git writes, no forbidden tokens; production changes only for a genuine bypass, each with its fixture.

Then write the Serena memory 'task-task-754fa988748b4d2abb2628f4c91d8ff5-handoff' for V12 (task-b621ddc9). Cover:
- the fixture classes and their exact codes and tokens;
- the createMcpCaller options parameter and the runnerCall pattern;
- any bypass fixed or reported;
- that V12 re-runs this file unchanged and should list src/__acceptance__ as an assertion root.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Daemon-side acceptance fixtures, all going through McpAdapter dispatch, prove that on a strict task forged, stale, missing, target-raced and crash-replayed evidence never satisfies qa_approve or a strict consumer's dependency. They are paired with a positive control that approves, plus the two CQ-V01 hand-forward tests.
acceptanceCriteria: A0 approves, and every bypass fixture differs from it by exactly one defect, asserting the exact codeName and tokens.
Forgery, stale, missing-check, target-race and receipt-crash classes are each covered in deliveryBypass.acceptance.test.ts.
W1 runs over the real /runner WebSocket; a wrong or missing key closes with 1008.
Both hand-forward tests kill their named mutants.
invariants: Production readiness is unchanged; verified-local is reachable only under this file's spy.
No tool handler is imported or called directly in the acceptance file.
The runner identity comes from authenticateRunner over the temp host key.
compatibility: createMcpCaller without options behaves exactly as V11 landed it.
approvedScope: a source fix only for a genuine bypass, each with its fixture
sourceAssumptions: server/McpAdapter.ts handle(request, options) forwards options.runner into the tool context.
server/WebSocketServer.ts handleMcpMessage passes the authenticated runner to mcpAdapter.handle.
state/receiptStore.ts allows one receipt per candidate, and an identical replay is a duplicate.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Importing V11's gatedApproval from producerConsumer.acceptance.test.ts: rejected. Importing a test module re-registers its suites. Also, gatedApproval uses legacy record_check_run evidence, which strict tasks must treat as forgery. A strict analogue lives in this file instead.
- Seeding evidence through the stores: rejected. Every call goes through McpAdapter. Runner-only tools are reached with createMcpCaller(state, adapter, { runner }), which is the exact dispatch WebSocketServer.handleMcpMessage uses, while W1 proves the real upgrade.
- A test-minted runner literal: rejected. The identity comes from authenticateRunner over the temp host key.
- A TDD red phase: not applicable. These are acceptance fixtures against landed code, so a red fixture means a bypass. A0's positive control prevents vacuous refusals.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Assumed interfaces, from approved plans (adapt to the landed names):
- V11: createMcpCaller(state, adapter?) returns { call, listTools }; McpCallError { code, codeName }.
- V03a: authenticateRunner(req, projectPath) returns RunnerIdentity or null; runnerId is runner-<16 hex of sha256(key)>; ensureRunnerKey returns the key FILE path; MOE_RUNNER_KEY_DIR; the /runner refusal closes with 1008 'runner authentication failed'.
- V03: record_check_dispatch takes { id?, taskId, candidateId, planRevision, command, checkId?, environment }. record_check_observation takes exactly { id, dispatchId, exitCode, outcome, outputTail, environment }; other keys are INVALID_INPUT, and a missing runner is RUNNER_CHANNEL_REQUIRED.
- V04: dispatch admission (CHECK_DEFINITION_NOT_APPROVED, CHECK_ENVIRONMENT_NOT_APPROVED); trustedPassedOn requires an authenticated passed run on the current candidate and tree, at the approved revision, in an approved environment.
- V05b: the observation result may carry `repair`; a code-failure would reopen the task, so no fixture uses one.
- V06: qa_approve { attemptId, generation, sessionId, candidateId }; codes STEP_ENTRY_IDENTITY_REQUIRED, ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED, CONTEXT_RECEIPT_STALE, CANDIDATE_MISMATCH, CANDIDATE_REVISION_STALE.
- V09: dependencyShortfall(state, id, consumer); 'archived-without-verified-delivery'; DEPENDENCY_EVIDENCE_MISSING on an explicit claim.

Verified precedents:
- McpAdapter.handle(request, { runner }) is what /runner calls.
- runnerChannel.test.ts W1 is the WebSocket harness.
- executionContract.e2e.test.ts provides strictInMemory and restartDaemon.
- planApproval.test.ts:1095 is the namespace readiness spy.
- receiptStore is keyed by candidateId, at most one receipt per candidate; a duplicate is idempotent.
- requiredChecks.delivery.test.ts has the helpers task(), missing(), candidate() and defs.
planningNotes.risks:
- Size: QA rejects past 400 net, and tests count. Keep the acceptance file to about 320 lines with it.each tables. A bypass fix that does not fit goes to report_blocked with a proposed split, never into an oversized diff.
- Vacuous refusals: always assert the exact codeName and tokens against A0's positive control.
- V05b side effects on observations (comments, alerts, retry-infra) must not be mistaken for qa_approve writes. Compare rows only around the qa_approve call.
- The order of V06's codes (binding before evidence) decides which code S1 and S3 see. Read the landed reviewBinding.test.ts first.
- Clean up env, spies, servers and sockets on every path. A restart needs fresh callers.
- verified-local is never enabled outside the spy, and production readiness is untouched.
- No wrapper changes; CQ-V08b owns those.
